sanskrit: na saṃkareṇa draviṇaṃ vicinvīta vicakṣaṇaḥ dharmārthaṃ nyāyam utsṛjya na tat kalyāṇam ucyate
english: The discerning man should not gather wealth by confusion of duties; to abandon the right way for the sake of dharma is not called auspicious.

sanskrit: sa tvam evaṃvidho dāntaḥ kṣatriyaḥ priyabāndhavaḥ prajā bhṛtyāṃś ca putrāṃś ca svadharmeṇānupālaya
english: Such a one as you are—self-controlled, a kṣatriya dear to your kinsmen—cherish your subjects, your dependents, and your sons in accordance with your own dharma.

sanskrit: iṣṭāniṣṭasamāyogo vairaṃ sauhārdam eva ca atha jātisahasrāṇi bahūni parivartate
english: Union with the pleasant and the unpleasant, enmity and likewise friendship—through many thousands of births these revolve again and again.

sanskrit: tasmād guṇeṣu rajyethā mā doṣeṣu kadā cana nirguṇo yo hi durbuddhir ātmanaḥ so 'rir ucyate
english: Therefore take delight in virtues, never in faults; for the man devoid of virtue and of evil mind is called his own enemy.

sanskrit: mānuṣeṣu mahārāja dharmādharmau pravartataḥ na tathānyeṣu bhūteṣu manuṣyarahiteṣv iha
english: Among human beings, O great king, dharma and adharma have their course; not so among the other creatures here that are devoid of human nature.

sanskrit: dharmaśīlo naro vidvān īhako 'nīhako 'pi vā ātmabhūtaḥ sadā loke cared bhūtāny ahiṃsayan
english: The learned man of righteous disposition, whether active in worldly effort or free from it, should always move through the world as one with all, harming no living being.

sanskrit: yadā vyapetahṛllekhaṃ mano bhavati tasya vai nānṛtaṃ caiva bhavati tadā kalyāṇam ṛcchati
english: When his mind has become free of all inner scruple and falsehood no longer dwells in him, then he attains the auspicious state.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca eṣa dharmavidhis tāta gṛhasthasya prakīrtitaḥ tapovidhiṃ tu vakṣyāmi tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: Parāśara said: This rule of dharma for the householder, my son, has now been declared; but I shall expound the rule of austerity—listen to me as I speak it.

sanskrit: prāyeṇa hi gṛhasthasya mamatvaṃ nāma jāyate saṅgāgataṃ naraśreṣṭha bhāvais tāmasarājasaiḥ
english: For in the householder, O best of men, there generally arises what is called "the sense of mine," born of attachment through states of tamas and rajas.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇy āśritya gāvaś ca kṣetrāṇi ca dhanāni ca dārāḥ putrāś ca bhṛtyāś ca bhavantīha narasya vai
english: Resting upon his house, a man comes to possess cattle, fields, and wealth, a wife, sons, and servants in this world.

sanskrit: evaṃ tasya pravṛttasya nityam evānupaśyataḥ rāgadveṣau vivardhete hy anityatvam apaśyataḥ
english: As he goes on thus, ever fixing his gaze upon these things and never perceiving their impermanence, his attraction and aversion grow and grow.

sanskrit: rāgadveṣābhibhūtaṃ ca naraṃ dravyavaśānugam mohajātā ratir nāma samupaiti narādhipa
english: And upon the man overwhelmed by attraction and aversion, enslaved to his possessions, there comes, O ruler of men, what is called delight, born of delusion.

sanskrit: kṛtārtho bhogato bhūtvā sa vai ratiparāyaṇaḥ lābhaṃ grāmyasukhād anyaṃ ratito nānupaśyati
english: Deeming himself fulfilled by enjoyment and wholly devoted to pleasure, he sees no gain from delight beyond that of vulgar comforts.

sanskrit: tato lobhābhibhūtātmā saṅgād vardhayate janam puṣṭyarthaṃ caiva tasyeha janasyārthaṃ cikīrṣati
english: Then, his soul overcome by greed, through attachment he increases his household, and he strives in this world to provide for the nourishment and welfare of that household.

sanskrit: sa jānann api cākāryam arthārthaṃ sevate naraḥ bālasnehaparītātmā tatkṣayāc cānutapyate
english: Though he knows it ought not to be done, the man pursues it for the sake of gain; his soul wrapped in fondness for his children, he grieves when that wealth is lost.

sanskrit: tato mānena saṃpanno rakṣann ātmaparājayam karoti yena bhogī syām iti tasmād vinaśyati
english: Then, filled with pride and guarding himself against defeat, he does whatever he thinks will make him an enjoyer of pleasures—and by this he comes to ruin.

sanskrit: tapo hi buddhiyuktānāṃ śāśvataṃ brahmadarśanam anvicchatāṃ śubhaṃ karma narāṇāṃ tyajatāṃ sukham
english: For austerity is the eternal vision of Brahman for those who are joined to wisdom—men who seek the auspicious work and renounce mere pleasure.

sanskrit: snehāyatananāśāc ca dhananāśāc ca pārthiva ādhivyādhipratāpāc ca nirvedam upagacchati
english: Through the loss of the objects of his affection, through the loss of wealth, O prince, and through the torment of mental and bodily afflictions, a man attains to disgust with the world.

sanskrit: nirvedād ātmasaṃbodhaḥ saṃbodhāc chāstradarśanam śāstrārthadarśanād rājaṃs tapa evānupaśyati
english: From world-weariness comes awakening to the self; from awakening, insight into scripture; and from perceiving the meaning of scripture, O king, he comes to behold austerity itself.

sanskrit: durlabho hi manuṣyendra naraḥ pratyavamarśavān yo vai priyasukhe kṣīṇe tapaḥ kartuṃ vyavasyati
english: Rare indeed, O lord of men, is the reflective man who, when his cherished happiness has waned, resolves to undertake austerity.

sanskrit: tapaḥ sarvagataṃ tāta hīnasyāpi vidhīyate jitendriyasya dāntasya svargamārgapradeśakam
english: Austerity, my son, is open to all, and is ordained even for the lowly; for one who has conquered his senses and is self-restrained, it points out the path to heaven.

sanskrit: prajāpatiḥ prajāḥ pūrvam asṛjat tapasā vibhuḥ kva cit kva cid vrataparo vratāny āsthāya pārthiva
english: In the beginning the lord Prajāpati created living beings through austerity, intent here and there upon vows, undertaking his observances, O prince.

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrās tathaivāgny aśvimārutāḥ viśvedevās tathā sādhyāḥ pitaro 'tha marudgaṇāḥ
english: The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, and likewise Agni, the Aśvins, and the Maruts, the Viśvedevas and the Sādhyas, the ancestors, and the host of the Maruts—

sanskrit: yakṣarākṣasagandharvāḥ siddhāś cānye divaukasaḥ saṃsiddhās tapasā tāta ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ
english: the Yakṣas, the Rākṣasas, the Gandharvas, the Siddhas, and the other dwellers in heaven—all were perfected through austerity, my son, as were the others who abide in heaven.

sanskrit: ye cādau brahmaṇā sṛṣṭā brāhmaṇās tapasā purā te bhāvayantaḥ pṛthivīṃ vicaranti divaṃ tathā
english: And the brāhmaṇas who were created at the beginning by Brahmā through austerity in days of old—they wander, sustaining the earth and likewise the heavens.

sanskrit: martyaloke ca rājāno ye cānye gṛhamedhinaḥ mahākuleṣu dṛśyante tat sarvaṃ tapasaḥ phalam
english: And the kings in the world of mortals, and the other householders who are seen in great families—all that is the fruit of austerity.

sanskrit: kauśikāni ca vastrāṇi śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca vāhanāsanayānāni sarvaṃ tat tapasaḥ phalam
english: Silken garments and lovely ornaments, mounts and seats and conveyances—all that is the fruit of austerity.

sanskrit: manonukūlāḥ pramadā rūpavatyaḥ sahasraśaḥ vāsaḥ prāsādapṛṣṭhe ca tat sarvaṃ tapasaḥ phalam
english: Lovely women, pleasing to the heart, by the thousands, and a dwelling upon the heights of a palace—all that is the fruit of austerity.

sanskrit: śayanāni ca mukhyāni bhojyāni vividhāni ca abhipretāni sarvāṇi bhavanti kṛtakarmaṇām
english: Choice couches and foods of many kinds—all things desired come to those who have performed the deed of austerity.

sanskrit: nāprāpyaṃ tapasā kiṃ cit trailokye 'smin paraṃtapa upabhogaparityāgaḥ phalāny akṛtakarmaṇām
english: There is nothing in these three worlds unattainable by austerity, O scorcher of foes; but the renunciation of all enjoyment is the only fruit of those who have done no such deed.

sanskrit: sukhito duḥkhito vāpi naro lobhaṃ parityajet avekṣya manasā śāstraṃ buddhyā ca nṛpasattama
english: Whether happy or sorrowful, a man should forsake greed, looking with his mind upon scripture and with his intellect, O best of kings.

sanskrit: asaṃtoṣo 'sukhāyaiva lobhād indriyavibhramaḥ tato 'sya naśyati prajñā vidyevābhyāsavarjitā
english: Discontent leads only to misery; from greed comes the bewilderment of the senses; and thereby his wisdom perishes, like learning bereft of practice.

sanskrit: naṣṭaprajño yadā bhavati tadā nyāyaṃ na paśyati tasmāt sukhakṣaye prāpte pumān ugraṃ tapaś caret
english: When a man's wisdom is destroyed, then he no longer perceives the right; therefore, when the loss of happiness has befallen him, let him practice fierce austerity.

sanskrit: yad iṣṭaṃ tat sukhaṃ prāhur dveṣyaṃ duḥkham ihocyate kṛtākṛtasya tapasaḥ phalaṃ paśyasva yādṛśam
english: What is desired they call happiness; what is hated is here called sorrow. Behold what kind the fruit is, of austerity done and undone.

sanskrit: nityaṃ bhadrāṇi paśyanti viṣayāṃś copabhuñjate prākāśyaṃ caiva gacchanti kṛtvā niṣkalmaṣaṃ tapaḥ
english: Those who have performed stainless austerity ever look upon blessings and enjoy the objects of sense, and they attain to renown.

sanskrit: apriyāṇy avamānāṃś ca duḥkhaṃ bahuvidhātmakam phalārthī satpathatyaktaḥ prāpnoti viṣayātmakam
english: But the seeker of reward who has forsaken the path of the good wins only what belongs to the senses—unpleasant things and dishonors and sorrow of many forms.

sanskrit: dharme tapasi dāne ca vicikitsāsya jāyate sa kṛtvā pāpakāny eva nirayaṃ pratipadyate
english: In him there arises doubt concerning dharma, austerity, and almsgiving; and having done only evil deeds, he attains to hell.

sanskrit: sukhe tu vartamāno vai duḥkhe vāpi narottama svavṛttād yo na calati śāstracakṣuḥ sa mānavaḥ
english: But whether dwelling in happiness or in sorrow, O best of men, the man who does not swerve from his own conduct—he is one whose eye is scripture.

sanskrit: iṣuprapātamātraṃ hi sparśayoge ratiḥ smṛtā rasane darśane ghrāṇe śravaṇe ca viśāṃ pate
english: In the union with touch, the delight lasts but the moment of an arrow's flight, and likewise in taste, in sight, in smell, and in hearing, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: tato 'sya jāyate tīvrā vedanā tatkṣayāt punaḥ budhā yena praśaṃsanti mokṣaṃ sukham anuttamam
english: Thereupon, when that delight has waned, sharp pain is born in him again—for which reason the wise extol liberation as the unsurpassed happiness.

sanskrit: tataḥ phalārthaṃ carati bhavanti jyāyaso guṇāḥ dharmavṛttyā ca satataṃ kāmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate
english: Then he acts for the sake of the fruit, and his virtues grow ever greater; and through righteous conduct he is never deprived of pleasure and prosperity.

sanskrit: aprayatnāgatāḥ sevyā gṛhasthair viṣayāḥ sadā prayatnenopagamyaś ca svadharma iti me matiḥ
english: The objects of sense, when they come without effort, may be enjoyed by householders; but it is one's own dharma that is to be sought with striving—such is my conviction.

sanskrit: mānināṃ kulajātānāṃ nityaṃ śāstrārthacakṣuṣām dharmakriyāviyuktānām aśaktyā saṃvṛtātmanām
english: For the proud, the high-born, those whose eye is ever upon the meaning of scripture, who are cut off from the performance of dharma and whose selves are hemmed in by helplessness—

sanskrit: kriyamāṇaṃ yadā karma nāśaṃ gacchati mānuṣam teṣāṃ nānyad ṛte loke tapasaḥ karma vidyate
english: when the human deed they undertake comes to naught, for them there is in this world no recourse but the work of austerity.

sanskrit: sarvātmanā tu kurvīta gṛhasthaḥ karmaniścayam dākṣyeṇa havyakavyārthaṃ svadharmaṃ vicaren nṛpa
english: With his whole soul let the householder hold firm to his resolve in works; with diligence, for the sake of offerings to gods and ancestors, let him follow his own dharma, O king.

sanskrit: yathā nadīnadāḥ sarve sāgare yānti saṃsthitim evam āśramiṇaḥ sarve gṛhasthe yānti saṃsthitim
english: As all rivers and streams come to their rest in the ocean, so all who follow the orders of life come to their rest in the householder.

sanskrit: janaka uvāca varṇo viśeṣavarṇānāṃ maharṣe kena jāyate etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tad brūhi vadatāṃ vara
english: Janaka said: From what, O great sage, does the class of the mixed classes arise? This I wish to hear; tell it to me, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: yad etaj jāyate 'patyaṃ sa evāyam iti śrutiḥ kathaṃ brāhmaṇato jāto viśeṣagrahaṇaṃ gataḥ
english: The scripture says that whatever offspring is born is the same as that from which it springs; how then has one born of a brāhmaṇa come to take on a distinct class?

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca evam etan mahārāja yena jātaḥ sa eva saḥ tapasas tv apakarṣeṇa jātigrahaṇatāṃ gataḥ
english: Parāśara said: It is even so, O great king: one is the same as that from which he is born; but through the falling away of austerity he has come to assume a separate caste.

sanskrit: sukṣetrāc ca subījāc ca puṇyo bhavati saṃbhavaḥ ato 'nyatarato hīnād avaro nāma jāyate
english: From a good field and from good seed a meritorious birth comes to be; but when either of the two is deficient, an inferior offspring is born.

sanskrit: vaktrād bhujābhyām ūrubhyāṃ padbhyāṃ caivātha jajñire sṛjataḥ prajāpater lokān iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: From the mouth, from the two arms, from the thighs, and from the feet they were born, as Prajāpati created the worlds—so the knowers of dharma understand.

sanskrit: mukhajā brāhmaṇās tāta bāhujāḥ kṣatrabandhavaḥ ūrujā dhanino rājan pādajāḥ paricārakāḥ
english: Born of the mouth are the brāhmaṇas, my son; born of the arms, the kindred of the kṣatriyas; born of the thighs, the men of wealth, O king; and born of the feet, the servants.

sanskrit: caturṇām eva varṇānām āgamaḥ puruṣarṣabha ato 'nye tv atiriktā ye te vai saṃkarajāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: There is a scriptural origin only for the four classes, O bull among men; those others who are over and above these are held to be born of intermixture.

sanskrit: kṣatrajātir athāmbaṣṭhā ugrā vaidehakās tathā śvapākāḥ pulkasāḥ stenā niṣādāḥ sūtamāgadhāḥ
english: The Kṣatrajātis, the Ambaṣṭhas, the Ugras, and likewise the Vaidehakas, the Śvapākas, the Pulkasas, the Stenas, the Niṣādas, the Sūtas, and the Māgadhas—

sanskrit: āyogāḥ karaṇā vrātyāś caṇḍālāś ca narādhipa ete caturbhyo varṇebhyo jāyante vai parasparam
english: the Āyogas, the Karaṇas, the Vrātyas, and the Caṇḍālas, O ruler of men—these are born from the four classes in mutual intermixture.

sanskrit: janaka uvāca brahmaṇaikena jātānāṃ nānātvaṃ gotrataḥ katham bahūnīha hi loke vai gotrāṇi munisattama
english: Janaka said: How can there be diversity of lineage among those born of the one Brahman? For there are indeed many lineages in this world, O best of sages.

sanskrit: yatra tatra kathaṃ jātāḥ svayoniṃ munayo gatāḥ śūdrayonau samutpannā viyonau ca tathāpare
english: How is it that the sages, born here and there—some sprung from a śūdra womb, and others from a womb other than their own—came to attain their own proper origin?

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca rājan naitad bhaved grāhyam apakṛṣṭena janmanā mahātmanāṃ samutpattis tapasā bhāvitātmanām
english: Parāśara said: O king, this is not to be taken as if the origin of the great-souled, whose selves are perfected by austerity, were defiled by a lowly birth.

sanskrit: utpādya putrān munayo nṛpate yatra tatra ha svenaiva tapasā teṣām ṛṣitvaṃ vidadhuḥ punaḥ
english: Having begotten sons here and there, O king, the sages, by their own austerity, conferred upon them once again the state of being seers.

sanskrit: pitāmahaś ca me pūrvam ṛśyaśṛṅgaś ca kāśyapaḥ vaṭas tāṇḍyaḥ kṛpaś caiva kakṣīvān kamaṭhādayaḥ
english: My grandfather of old, and Ṛśyaśṛṅga, and Kaśyapa, Vaṭa, Tāṇḍya, and Kṛpa, Kakṣīvān, Kamaṭha, and the rest—

sanskrit: yavakrītaś ca nṛpate droṇaś ca vadatāṃ varaḥ āyur mataṅgo dattaś ca drupado matsya eva ca
english: and Yavakrīta, O king, and Droṇa, best of speakers, Āyu, Mataṅga, Datta, Drupada, and Matsya as well—

sanskrit: ete svāṃ prakṛtiṃ prāptā vaideha tapaso ''śrayāt pratiṣṭhitā vedavido dame tapasi caiva hi
english: these, O Vaideha, attained their own true nature through reliance upon austerity; knowers of the Veda, they stood firm in self-restraint and in austerity.

sanskrit: mūlagotrāṇi catvāri samutpannāni pārthiva aṅgirāḥ kaśyapaś caiva vasiṣṭho bhṛgur eva ca
english: Four root-lineages came into being, O prince: Aṅgiras and Kaśyapa, Vasiṣṭha and Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: karmato 'nyāni gotrāṇi samutpannāni pārthiva nāmadheyāni tapasā tāni ca grahaṇaṃ satām
english: The other lineages arose from works, O prince—they are but names, and through austerity they too win acceptance among the good.

sanskrit: janaka uvāca viśeṣadharmān varṇānāṃ prabrūhi bhagavan mama tathā sāmānyadharmāṃś ca sarvatra kuśalo hy asi
english: Janaka said: Declare to me, O blessed one, the particular duties of the classes, and likewise their common duties; for you are skilled in all things.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca pratigraho yājanaṃ ca tathaivādhyāpanaṃ nṛpa viśeṣadharmo viprāṇāṃ rakṣā kṣatrasya śobhanā
english: Parāśara said: Receiving gifts, officiating at sacrifices, and likewise teaching, O king, are the particular duties of the brāhmaṇas; protection is the glory of the kṣatriya.

sanskrit: kṛṣiś ca pāśupālyaṃ ca vāṇijyaṃ ca viśām api dvijānāṃ paricaryā ca śūdrakarma narādhipa
english: Tillage, the herding of cattle, and trade belong to the vaiśyas; and the service of the twice-born is the work of the śūdra, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: viśeṣadharmā nṛpate varṇānāṃ parikīrtitāḥ dharmān sādhāraṇāṃs tāta vistareṇa śṛṇuṣva me
english: The particular duties of the classes have now been proclaimed, O king; now hear from me at length, my son, the duties common to all.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyam ahiṃsā cāpramādaḥ saṃvibhāgitā śrāddhakarmātitheyaṃ ca satyam akrodha eva ca
english: Freedom from cruelty, non-injury, vigilance, the sharing of one's goods, the rites for the ancestors, hospitality, truthfulness, and freedom from anger—

sanskrit: sveṣu dāreṣu saṃtoṣaḥ śaucaṃ nityānasūyatā ātmajñānaṃ titikṣā ca dharmāḥ sādhāraṇā nṛpa
english: contentment with one's own wife, purity, constant freedom from envy, knowledge of the self, and forbearance—these are the common duties, O king.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyās trayo varṇā dvijātayaḥ atra teṣām adhīkāro dharmeṣu dvipadāṃ vara
english: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas—these three classes are the twice-born; among these their entitlement lies in the sacred duties, O best of two-footed beings.

sanskrit: vikarmāvasthitā varṇāḥ patanti nṛpate trayaḥ unnamanti yathāsantam āśrityeha svakarmasu
english: The three classes, when settled in forbidden works, fall low, O king; but they rise up by resorting, as is fitting, to their own proper works here.

sanskrit: na cāpi śūdraḥ patatīti niścayo; na cāpi saṃskāram ihārhatīti vā śrutipravṛttaṃ na ca dharmam āpnute; na cāsya dharme pratiṣedhanaṃ kṛtam
english: And it is settled that the śūdra does not fall low, nor is he entitled here to the sacraments; he does not attain to the dharma that proceeds from scripture, yet no prohibition of dharma has been laid upon him.

sanskrit: vaidehakaṃ śūdram udāharanti; dvijā mahārāja śrutopapannāḥ ahaṃ hi paśyāmi narendra devaṃ; viśvasya viṣṇuṃ jagataḥ pradhānam
english: The twice-born who are versed in scripture cite the example of the Vaidehaka śūdra, O great king; for I behold, O lord of men, the god Viṣṇu, the foremost principle of the whole universe.

sanskrit: satāṃ vṛttam anuṣṭhāya nihīnā ujjihīrṣavaḥ mantravarjaṃ na duṣyanti kurvāṇāḥ pauṣṭikīḥ kriyāḥ
english: By following the conduct of the good, the lowly who long to lift themselves up are not defiled when they perform the rites of prosperity, save for the use of the sacred mantras.

sanskrit: yathā yathā hi sadvṛttam ālambantītare janāḥ tathā tathā sukhaṃ prāpya pretya ceha ca śerate
english: In just the measure that other folk take hold of the conduct of the good, in that same measure do they win happiness and repose at ease, both here and after death.

sanskrit: janaka uvāca kiṃ karma dūṣayaty enam atha jātir mahāmune saṃdeho me samutpannas tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Janaka said: Is it conduct that defiles a man, or birth, O great sage? A doubt has arisen in me; this you should explain to me.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca asaṃśayaṃ mahārāja ubhayaṃ doṣakārakam karma caiva hi jātiś ca viśeṣaṃ tu niśāmaya
english: Parāśara said: Without doubt, O great king, both are makers of defilement—both conduct and birth; but mark the distinction.

sanskrit: jātyā ca karmaṇā caiva duṣṭaṃ karma niṣevate jātyā duṣṭaś ca yaḥ pāpaṃ na karoti sa pūruṣaḥ
english: He who, by birth and by conduct alike, pursues defiled deeds is corrupt; but he who, though base by birth, does no evil—he is the true man.

sanskrit: jātyā pradhānaṃ puruṣaṃ kurvāṇaṃ karma dhikkṛtam karma tad dūṣayaty enaṃ tasmāt karma naśobhanam
english: When a man eminent by birth performs a deed that is to be condemned, that deed defiles him; therefore it is the deed that is not fair.
